@graph.name: AI Publicist — Fractional Senior Operator
@graph.description: A fractional senior AI publicist who knows the AI beat, the editors who cover it, and how to position a technical product as a business story. Placements include Forbes, Decrypt, Benzinga and a six-podcast tour for Gaia AI. Works at $5K–$12K/month versus $15K–$45K/month agency retainers, with GEO and AEO visibility built in.

mainEntity.name: What does an AI publicist actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI publicist handles the full press and visibility strategy for an AI company: narrative positioning, journalist outreach to AI and tech beats, podcast booking, embargo management, and building the structured citation footprint that gets your company named in ChatGPT and Perplexity answers. The difference from a generalist PR person is deep familiarity with the AI beat, the outlets that cover it seriously, and the language that lands with editors at Forbes, Decrypt, The Information and MIT Tech Review.

mainEntity.name: How much does an AI publicist cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional AI PR agency typically charges $15K–$45K per month because the retainer covers a multi-person account team. A fractional senior AI publicist like Shilika Jain runs the same senior scope for $5K–$12K per month. A focused launch sprint, covering a funding announcement or product release, runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks. The right tier depends on whether you need ongoing narrative building or a single high-stakes moment.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets can an AI publicist get me into?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tier-1 tech and AI: Forbes, The Information, MIT Technology Review, Wired, VentureBeat, TechCrunch. Crypto-adjacent AI: Decrypt, CoinDesk, Blockworks, The Defiant. Financial and business: Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga. Regional tech where relevant: Inc42 (India), e27 (SEA), Tech in Asia. The specific list depends on your story and the news hook. A wire blast to all of them produces nothing; a tailored pitch to the right editor at the right moment produces a placement.

mainEntity.name: What is the process and how long does it take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks cover an audit of your current press footprint and a positioning session that produces your category claim and founder thesis. Weeks three and four are active outreach, with pitches built for specific editors and podcast hosts booked where relevant. A first tier-1 placement typically lands within four to six weeks of kick-off, assuming a real news hook exists. Ongoing retainer work compounds from there.

mainEntity.name: How do I start working with you?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send a short project brief through the intent form and you will get a reply within 24 hours with a quick read on your current press footprint and whether the timing is right. Alternatively, book a 30-minute call at https://calendly.com/shilikajain/30min/ and we will assess the opportunity live. No deck required, no account-team intro call.
